mainTopic: The morning ash removal, the גמרא on porticoes in the עזרה and the timing of the חביתין, and the start of the next פרק on clearing the מזבח
overview: This amud first finishes the משנה's account of the morning clearing of ashes. The waiting כהנים heard the sound of בן קטין's machine for the כיור, and the chosen כהן washed, went up with a silver pan, scooped out the burnt inner coals, and piled them on the floor near the ramp. The גמרא then asks how there could be porticoes (אכסדראות) in the עזרה, when a ברייתא forbids any tree near the מזבח. רב חסדא answers that the משנה means porticoes built of stone. Next the גמרא asks whether the חביתין came before the תמיד של שחר, which must be the first offering of the day. רב יהודה answers that the early step was only heating water for the חביתין. The first פרק then ends. A new משנה describes the other כהנים rushing up the מזבח, moving unburnt limbs and fats aside, and piling the ashes onto the תפוח, which was left in place on the רגלים as a נוי למזבח. The משנה's last sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The signal of the כיור machine and the כהן going up to the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes how the waiting כהנים knew it was time, and how the chosen כהן washed and went up the מזבח with a silver pan.
steps.simpleTranslation: The other כהנים could not hear him moving until they heard the noise of the wooden machine בן קטין made for the כיור. Then they said, 'The time has come!' The כהן washed his hands and feet from the כיור, took the silver coal pan, and went up to the top of the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its step-by-step account of the morning ash removal. The noise of the כיור machine tells everyone that the כהן is about to start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The chosen כהן went off alone, so the others could not track him. The sound of בן קטין's machine raising the כיור was their signal. Before any service he must wash his hands and feet from the כיור, and only then does he take the silver pan and go up.

keyTerms.meaning: The basin in the courtyard used by כהנים to wash hands and feet
A machine or mechanism, here the wooden device for the כיור
The required washing of hands and feet before Temple service
A coal pan used to scoop coals or ashes

phrases.english: And they would not hear his sound,
phrases.notes: The other כהנים are waiting, and they can't hear the chosen כהן who went off alone.

phrases.english: until they would hear the sound of the wood
that בן קטין made into a machine for the basin.
phrases.notes: This was a pulley device that lowered the כיור into water overnight and raised it in the morning.

phrases.english: And they would say: The time has come!
He sanctified his hands and his feet from the basin,
he took the silver coal pan
and went up to the top of the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's description from the previous section of the daf
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן washes from the כיור when its machine is heard, takes the silver pan, and goes up the מזבח.

steps.title: Scooping the coals and piling them by the ramp
steps.stepSummary: The כהן scoops out the inner burnt coals, goes down, walks about ten אמות along the ramp, and piles the coals at the set place on the floor.
steps.simpleTranslation: He pushed the coals to the sides and scooped up the fully burnt coals from the inside. He went down to the floor, turned to face north, and walked about ten אמות along the east side of the ramp. He piled the coals on the floor three טפחים away from the ramp. This was the same place where they put the crop of the bird offering, the ashes of the inner מזבח, and the ashes of the מנורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes the actual ash removal: what the כהן scoops and exactly where he puts it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He takes only the inner, fully burnt coals. The spot where he piles them is precise, three טפחים from the ramp. It is also the shared place for other Temple waste: the bird's crop and the ashes of the inner מזבח and the מנורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Coals
The ramp leading up to the מזבח
The floor of the courtyard
The crop of a bird offering, which is removed and thrown aside
Removal of ashes

steps.whatToRemember: The ashes from תרומת הדשן were placed on the floor three טפחים east of the ramp, in the same spot used for the bird's crop and the ashes of the inner מזבח and the מנורה.

phrases.english: He cleared the coals to this side and that side,
scooping up the inner ones that were fully burnt.
He went down and reached the floor,
he turned his face to the north,

phrases.aramaic: הוֹלֵךְ בְּמִזְרָחוֹ שֶׁל כֶּבֶשׁ כְּעֶשֶׂר אַמּוֹת.
phrases.english: walking along the east side of the ramp about ten cubits.

phrases.aramaic: צָבַר אֶת הַגֶּחָלִים עַל גַּבֵּי הָרִצְפָּה
phrases.english: He piled the coals on the floor
three handbreadths away from the ramp,
the place where they put the crop of the bird,
and the ashes removed from the inner altar,
and the ashes removed from the Menorah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same sequence: after going up, he scoops and deposits the coals
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The inner burnt coals are scooped and piled on the floor three טפחים from the ramp, in the shared disposal spot.

steps.title: Were porticoes allowed in the courtyard at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's mention of an אכסדרה in the עזרה, using a ברייתא that forbids building porticoes there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Were there really porticoes in the עזרה? But a ברייתא teaches that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: How do we know we may not build porticoes in the עזרה? The פסוק says, 'Do not plant for yourself an אשרה of any tree near the מזבח of ה׳ your God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It challenges a detail from earlier in the משנה, where the כהנים walked along an אכסדרה in the עזרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה assumes a portico stood in the עזרה. But רבי אליעזר בן יעקב learns from a פסוק that porticoes may not be built there. So the משנה seems to clash with the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: A portico, a roofed walkway with columns
The Temple courtyard
A tree used for idol worship
'The פסוק teaches,' introducing the source for a law
'And were there really...?', a challenging question

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about anything in this section's משנה lines. It points back to an earlier line of the משנה that mentioned the אכסדרה.

phrases.english: GEMARA: And were there porticoes in the courtyard?
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says:
From where do we know that one may not build porticoes in the courtyard?
The verse teaches:
"You shall not plant for yourself an אשרה

phrases.aramaic: כָּל עֵץ אֵצֶל מִזְבַּח ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ״,
phrases.english: of any tree beside the altar of ה׳ your God."

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי הֲווֹ אַכְסַדְרָאוֹת בָּעֲזָרָה? וְהָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא by challenging a detail mentioned earlier in the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's assumption that there was an אכסדרה in the עזרה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא derives from a פסוק that building porticoes in the עזרה is forbidden, so the משנה's portico seems impossible.

steps.title: How the פסוק forbids any tree near the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains how the ברייתא reads the פסוק: it holds two separate bans, one on an אשרה and one on any tree near the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the פסוק means: 'Do not plant an אשרה,' and also, 'Do not plant any tree near the מזבח of ה׳ your God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the ברייתא's reading of the פסוק. This makes the challenge against the משנה stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, the פסוק only bans an idol tree. The ברייתא splits it into two bans. The second one forbids any wood near the מזבח, and porticoes were usually made of wood.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is what it is saying,' introducing an explanation of a text
Any tree or wood

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
"You shall not plant for yourself an אשרה,"

phrases.aramaic: ״לֹא תִטַּע לְךָ כׇּל עֵץ אֵצֶל מִזְבַּח ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ״!
phrases.english: and "You shall not plant for yourself any tree beside the altar of ה׳ your God"!
phrases.notes: Since porticoes were usually wooden, this second ban is what rules them out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the ברייתא's פסוק supports its law, finishing the challenge
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's portico in the עזרה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק, read as two bans, forbids any wood near the מזבח, which would include a wooden portico.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the משנה means stone porticoes
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that the משנה's porticoes were made of building materials like stone, which the פסוק does not forbid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: The משנה is talking about porticoes made of building materials, such as stone.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא resolves the challenge. He explains which kind of portico the משנה means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban comes from the words 'any tree,' so it only covers wooden porticoes. A portico built of stone is not a tree, so the פסוק does not forbid it. That way the משנה and the ברייתא do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Building, here meaning built from construction materials such as stone

steps.whatToRemember: Wooden porticoes are forbidden in the עזרה because of 'any tree near the מזבח.' Stone porticoes are allowed, and that is what the משנה means.

phrases.english: רב חסדא said:
It is referring to porticoes made of building materials.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: בְּאַכְסַדְרָאוֹת שֶׁל בִּנְיָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in steps 3 and 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the משנה refers to a different type of portico than the one the ברייתא forbids
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's portico was a wooden one, which would break the ban on any tree near the מזבח
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's portico was made of stone, and the ban covers only wooden porticoes

steps.title: Did the griddle-cake offering come first?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes an earlier line of the משנה and asks if it means the חביתין were done before everything else.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'They would keep inspecting...' Does this mean the חביתין offering came first?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to an earlier line in the משנה and raises a question about it. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the inspecting כהנים told the חביתין maker to start working very early. That makes it sound like the חביתין were offered before the other services of the day. The גמרא wants to check whether that is really true.

keyTerms.meaning: The כהן גדול's daily griddle-cake offering
'Is this to say...?' The גמרא is drawing out what a statement implies
Came first, were done earlier

phrases.english: [The משנה said:] They would keep inspecting, etc.
Is this to say that the griddle-cake offering came first?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. It returns to an earlier line of the משנה, not to the אכסדרה discussion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the משנה mean the חביתין were offered before the תמיד של שחר?

steps.title: Nothing may come before the morning offering
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches from a פסוק that nothing is offered before the תמיד של שחר. That seems to clash with the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: How do we know that nothing comes before the morning תמיד? The פסוק says 'and he shall arrange the עולה on it.' And רבה said: 'the עולה' means the first עולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge what the משנה seemed to say. The ברייתא says the morning תמיד must be the very first offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learns this from the word 'הָעֹלָה' in the פסוק. רבה explains that 'the עולה,' with the word 'the,' points to the first and main עולה of the day. So if the חביתין came first, the משנה would go against this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily morning קרבן תמיד
From where do we know?
The first עולה, the one that opens the day

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: From where do we know that nothing
comes before the daily morning offering?
The verse says: "And he shall arrange the burnt offering upon it,"
and Rabba said: "The burnt offering" means the first burnt offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the question of step 6 into a real contradiction by bringing a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's sign that the חביתין were prepared first
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא and רבה say the תמיד של שחר must be first. So the חביתין cannot come before it.

steps.title: They only heated water early
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers that the early step for the חביתין was only heating water to scald them. It was not offering them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: They told him to start so he could heat hot water for scalding the cakes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the challenge. The חביתין maker was not offering anything yet. He was only getting hot water ready.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חביתין had to be scalded in hot water before they were baked, and heating water takes time. So the early start was only preparation. The חביתין were still offered after the תמיד, and the ברייתא's rule holds.

keyTerms.meaning: To heat hot water
Scalding the flour mixture in hot water, part of making the חביתין

steps.whatToRemember: The תמיד של שחר is always the first offering of the day. Early work for the חביתין was only preparation, like heating water.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
[It was] to heat hot water for the scalding.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: לְהָחֵם חַמִּין לִרְבִיכָה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines what the early activity was
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Starting the חביתין early meant they were offered first.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the hot-water preparation started early. The offering itself came after the תמיד.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק בשלשה מקומות
steps.stepSummary: The first פרק of the מסכת ends with the traditional closing line.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק בשלשה מקומות.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional closing line said at the end of a פרק. Here it ends the first פרק of the מסכת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פרק is named for its opening words, 'בשלשה מקומות.' The line closes it, and a new פרק starts right after.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We will return to you.' The closing line at the end of a פרק
'In three places.' The name of the פרק that is ending

phrases.english: We will return to you, "In Three Places"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the whole פרק after the last answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The first פרק is finished, and a new פרק begins.

steps.title: The other priests rush up the altar
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה describes how the other כהנים saw the first כהן come down, washed quickly at the כיור, and climbed the מזבח with shovels and forks.
steps.simpleTranslation: His fellow כהנים saw that he had come down, and they came running. They quickly washed their hands and feet from the כיור, took the shovels and the forks, and went up to the top of the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It picks up right where the story stopped: the first כהן has come down with the coals, and now the others rush in to help.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before any service, the כהנים must wash their hands and feet from the כיור. They then take two kinds of tools up to the top of the מזבח: shovels and forks.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. It marks the start of a new משנה
His brothers. Here it means his fellow כהנים
Shovels
Forks

phrases.english: MISHNA: His brethren saw that he had come down,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the כהן from the last משנה who scooped out the coals and came down from the מזבח.

phrases.english: and they would run and come.

phrases.aramaic: מִהֲרוּ וְקִדְּשׁוּ יְדֵיהֶם וְרַגְלֵיהֶם מִן הַכִּיּוֹר,
phrases.english: They hurried and sanctified their hands and feet from the Basin,
they took the shovels and the forks
and went up to the top of the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new פרק and continues the story of the morning service.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the coals are taken out, the other כהנים wash at the כיור and climb the מזבח with shovels and forks.

steps.title: Moving unburnt limbs and fats to the sides of the altar
steps.stepSummary: Limbs and fats that did not finish burning from the night before are pushed to the sides of the מזבח. If the sides are too full, they are arranged on the כבש, opposite the סובב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The limbs and fats that had not burned up since the evening were moved to the sides of the מזבח. If the sides could not hold them all, they were arranged on the ramp, opposite the ledge around the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps describing the morning work. It tells us what the כהנים did with pieces of קרבנות that were still on the fire from the night before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהנים needed to clear the middle of the מזבח for the ashes and the new fire. The leftover אברים and פדרים are not thrown out, because they still need to finish burning. They are only moved aside, and if there is no room, they go on the כבש, opposite the סובב.

keyTerms.meaning: Limbs, the body parts of a קרבן that are burned on the מזבח
Fats of the קרבן that are burned on the מזבח
Were burned up, fully consumed by the fire
The ledge that runs around the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: Moving the pieces aside does not mean they are being thrown away. They stay on the מזבח so they can keep burning.

phrases.english: The limbs and the fats
that were not consumed since the evening –
they move them to the sides of the altar.
If the sides cannot hold them –
they arrange them on the ramp, opposite the surrounding ledge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's description of the כהנים' work after they climbed the מזבח with shovels and forks.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unburnt limbs and fats from the night are moved to the sides of the מזבח, or onto the כבש opposite the סובב if the sides are full.

steps.title: Piling the ashes onto the heap in the middle of the altar
steps.stepSummary: The כהנים began lifting the ashes onto the תפוח, a big heap in the center of the מזבח that sometimes held about three hundred כור.
steps.simpleTranslation: They began lifting the ashes up onto the heap. The heap was in the middle of the מזבח, and sometimes there were about three hundred כור of ashes on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes the next job: shoveling the ashes onto a central pile called the תפוח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is new information about where the ashes go. They are not taken off the מזבח right away. They are collected onto a heap in the middle, and the heap could grow very large, up to about three hundred כור.

keyTerms.meaning: Ashes left from the fire on the מזבח
The round heap of ashes in the middle of the מזבח (literally 'apple')
A large measure of volume

phrases.english: They began bringing up the ashes
onto the heap.
The heap was in the middle of the altar.
Sometimes there was on it
about three hundred kor.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵחֵלּוּ מַעֲלִין בָּאֵפֶר עַל גַּב תַּפּוּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the leftover pieces are moved aside, the משנה moves on to the ashes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ashes are lifted onto the תפוח, a central heap on the מזבח that could hold about three hundred כור.

steps.title: On the festivals the heap was left as a beauty for the altar
steps.stepSummary: On the רגלים the כהנים did not clear away the תפוח, because the heap was a נוי for the מזבח. The משנה then begins a new sentence with the word ומימיו.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the festivals they did not clear the heap away, because it was a beauty for the מזבח. And in all its days...
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a special rule for the רגלים: the ash heap stays in place. The last word begins the next sentence, which continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On ordinary days a heap that grew too big would be cleared off. On the רגלים it was left, because a large heap was considered a נוי למזבח, showing how many קרבנות were brought there. The final word ומימיו opens a new statement about the מזבח that the משנה finishes later.

keyTerms.meaning: The three pilgrimage festivals: פסח, שבועות, סוכות
Clearing away the ashes
A beauty or adornment for the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: The ashes are gathered onto the תפוח in the middle of the מזבח. On the רגלים the heap is left in place because it is a נוי למזבח.

phrases.english: And on the festivals they would not clear it away,
because it was a beauty for the altar.
And in all its days

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a festival exception about the תפוח that was just described.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the רגלים the ash heap was not cleared, because it was a נוי למזבח.
